title: Unlearning or Obfuscating? Jogging the Memory of Unlearned LLMs via Benign Relearning
forget_metric: attack success rate; Rouge-L; LLM-judge score
near_collapse_behaviour: deeper unlearning (more steps) lowers relearn success: 100%->48%->8% in toy sweep
notes: 15 GPT-generated benign articles per WMDP question restore LLM-judge score 1.27->6.2 (= original model) for GA; NPO 1.0->5.08. Relearn set contains none of the forgotten text.

title: Eight Methods to Evaluate Robust Unlearning in LLMs
notes: WHP knowledge recoverable via jailbreaks; in-context relearning; fine-tuning on related text; latent probing — unlearning is shallow suppression not removal.

title: Do Unlearning Methods Remove Information from Language Model Weights?
notes: Fine-tuning on half the forgotten facts recovers >=88% of accuracy on the OTHER disjoint half — information hidden not removed; strong prior that healing-adjacent FT resurfaces.

title: Catastrophic Failure of LLM Unlearning via Quantization
near_collapse_behaviour: 4-bit quantization restores hidden knowledge because unlearning weight deltas are small
notes: 21% forget knowledge retained at fp16 -> 83% after 4-bit quant for utility-constrained methods. Mitigation SURE: saliency-based larger-magnitude updates.

title: Towards LLM Unlearning Resilient to Relearning Attacks: A Sharpness-Aware Minimization Perspective and Beyond
near_collapse_behaviour: VerbMem recovers faster than KnowMem under relearning
notes: 20 forget samples x1 epoch: NPO UE 0.74->0.57 vs NPO+SAM 0.74->0.70. 3 epochs x20 samples: NPO 0.37 vs NPO+SAM 0.59. Flat-minima unlearning resists relearning.

title: Unlearning Isn't Deletion: Investigating Reversibility of Machine Unlearning in LLMs
near_collapse_behaviour: aggressive LR (3e-5) over 50-100 sequential requests -> irreversible catastrophic collapse; final recovery only 1-4%
notes: KEY for H2: relearning on unrelated data -> minimal recovery; retain-set -> moderate slower recovery; forget-set -> fastest (~77-100%). 100 sequential requests studied; moderate settings stay reversible (~80-82% recovery).

title: From Dormant to Deleted: Tamper-Resistant Unlearning Through Weight-Space Regularization
method_family: weight-space regularization (Weight Distortion / WeightDistReg / L1-sparse) vs behavioural (SCRUB/NegGrad+/Circuit Breakers)
notes: CAUTION for healing pass: retain-set-ONLY fine-tuning recovers forget acc ~50%->~100% for vulnerable methods (retrain-from-scratch stays ~50%); weight-space regularized methods resist. Vision-domain evidence.

title: Unlearning That Lasts: Utility-Preserving Robust and Almost Irreversible Forgetting in LLMs (JensUn)
near_collapse_behaviour: GradDiff at 2k steps: 0% recovery but utility collapse (WR=0.03)
notes: 600 steps of benign FT on UNRELATED data: JensUn (2k unlearn steps) recovers to only 8% forget acc vs NPO 26% and NPO+SAM 58%. Longer unlearning hardens resistance. 3-4B models = project scale.

title: Measure Don't Optimize: Forecasting Recovery in LLM Unlearning (J-Access)
method_family: recovery-forecast audit over 8 families (GradDiff NPO SimNPO AltPO IdkDPO IdkNLL UNDIAL RMU)
notes: Deep-deletion variants (GradDiff RMU) show post-attack revival 0.000-0.025 vs 0.695-0.800 for shallow variants. Pre-attack J-Access predicts steps-to-recover (Spearman rho=-0.70) — usable as cheap pre-healing audit.

title: Distillation Robustifies Unlearning (UNDO)
notes: Unlearn+distill matches data-filtered-oracle relearning resistance under 500 relearn steps; tunable compute-vs-robustness Pareto. Distillation is a candidate deep-heal stage.

title: Rethinking Benign Relearning: Syntax as the Hidden Driver of Unlearning Failures
method_family: attack analysis + syntactic diversification of forget set
notes: Syntactically similar relearn data: ~60-80% keyword recovery; topically similar: ~0-20%. Mitigation: paraphrasing forget queries (syntactic similarity 0.45->0.22) eliminates benign-relearning vulnerability — direct guidance for filtering healing data by FORM not just topic.

title: Tamper-Resistant Safeguards for Open-Weight LLMs (TAR)
method_family: adversarial meta-learning over simulated fine-tuning attacks
near_collapse_behaviour: high compute; utility costs reported by follow-ups
notes: Resists hundreds of fine-tuning attack steps where baselines (e.g. RMU) break within a few; meta-learning training loop likely too heavy for a 4B single-GPU daily cadence.

title: On Large Language Model Continual Unlearning (O3)
method_family: orthogonal LoRA + OOD detector for sequential requests
near_collapse_behaviour: errors accumulate across sequential rounds without mitigation
notes: Sequential unlearning cost grows near-linearly per request; naive repetition accumulates utility damage — relevant to touch-up cost trajectory though not same-item re-suppression.

title: Robust LLM Unlearning Against Relearning Attacks: The Minor Components in Representations Matter
method_family: representation-space: push unlearning into minor PCA components
notes: Mechanism finding: unlearning concentrates changes in dominant representation components and relearning preferentially restores exactly those — generic explanation for fast recovery across methods.
